_comment: Single source of truth for the verification-suite table rendered into
README.md (round-8 codex recommendation: the table rows drifted from
the artifacts twice; now scripts/gen_verification_table.py renders the
table from this file, and test_regressions.py both re-renders it in
check mode and compares the counters below against the artifacts that
generate them). Until round 15 the table was rendered into both
paper/main.md and paper/main.tex; the paper's Section 4.4 now points
at README.md and the tex templates are gone.
Counters are numbers cited anywhere in prose; rows reference them as
{name} placeholders so a number lives in exactly one place.
Each row's `literals` lists every digit-run that legitimately appears
verbatim in its templates (constants, file names, section numbers);
gen_verification_table.py fails if the templates carry any other digits.
Round 11 (P11-1/2) showed the digit audit alone is NOT enough: a counter
retyped as a digit already declared in `literals` passed, and swapping two
placeholders inside a row passed. Each row's `placeholders` therefore
declares the exact ORDERED sequence of counter names its templates carry,
and `cells` how many of them each cell carries (round 12, P12-7: a
counter moved across a cell boundary is a different table);
gen_verification_table.py fails unless the md cells and both
declarations agree, order included. test_regressions.py drills the
historical mutations against the validators every run.

md: {brute_force_base} + {brute_force_sharp} instances × 3 defence variants (`hold`, literal `(‡)`, attacking + `NO_RETALIATION`); the 3-PARTITION tier is m = 2 only, {brute_force_tri_yes} yes / {brute_force_tri_no} no

{dp_random_instances} random instances against exhaustive knapsack search, {dp_game_instances} single-creature corridors played out exhaustively in the game model, plus a multi-creature negative control
agrees everywhere; the control disagrees, exactly as Proposition 1.1's hypotheses require

{featureless_runs} instance runs, `m ∈ {2,3}`, two defence variants, through the tiers C1–C5 (reachability, separation, every balanced assignment simulated, the arithmetic relaxation, saturation); plus the exhaustive play tier C6 — targets AND approach hexes, a passing stack may vanish — on the {featureless_c6_instances} smallest legal instances (`T = 13`, one yes and one no) × {featureless_c6_allocs} allocations each
no mismatches; C6's exact maximum decides 3-PARTITION and never exceeds the relaxation

C6 on all {featureless_c6_full_instances} smallest legal instances (`T ∈ {13, 16}`, two yes, two no) × {featureless_c6_allocs} allocations; outside the battery, which pins the instance list's length in-process
{x3c_full_vacate_built} instances ({x3c_full_vacate_yes} yes, {x3c_full_vacate_no} no), `q ≤ 4`, {x3c_full_vacate_skipped} skipped by the router

{crosscheck_full_built} machine-built planar boards ({crosscheck_full_yes} yes, {crosscheck_full_no} no), {crosscheck_full_skipped} skipped by the router, under the **published** Theorem 3 constants (`def 27`, `hp 4`, `μ = 0.35`)
{crosscheck_default_instances} instances, published constants AND literal `(‡)` — the combination round 8 found had never been run

{free_order_built} boards — one corpus of eight q = 2 families, each built and searched under BOTH the historical (def 41) and the published (def 27) constants, the swap asserted at build time — searched with free activation order (any unacted player stack may act next), pass and vanish branches and exhaustive approach hexes, over every allocation ({free_order_yes} yes / {free_order_no} no builds), under the `hold` defence, which dominates (‡) for the player

the free-order answer equals X3C and the fixed order on every (family, constant set, allocation) triple; yes-instances admit only the all-ones winner; {free_order_controls} discriminating controls — order, vanish, destination — on which the full search strictly beats its degraded variants; the negative control (defence = attack) flips {free_order_flips} planar no-instance to yes; the corpus tiers expanded {free_order_reorder} out-of-order activations and {free_order_vanish} vanish branches and met {free_order_multispot} states offering a second approach hex — Lemma D.7 from the searcher's side, so the destination branch is exercised by its control only

{lemma_families} corpus families through the Lemma D.4 embedding algorithm itself (DMP planarity → orthogonal drawing → `λ = 20` scaling, adapters, stubs): {lemma_built} boards built; {lemma_degenerate_no} certified degenerate no-instances, {lemma_degenerate_nonplanar} of them also non-planar; {lemma_nonplanar} certified non-planar — plus a separate battery of {lemma_malformed} malformed encodings and one planted non-planar control, all deterministic

I1–I4, the Lemma D.4 feature counts (4|C| boxes, 6|C| − |X| corridors) and the feature-based (SEP′) separation hold on every board ({sep_pairs} non-incident feature pairs, class minima L∞ {sep_min_bb}/{sep_min_bc}/{sep_min_cc} against the required {sep_required}); the no-certificate board, assembled from its own encoding, plays out as a genuine no; the full game search runs on {lemma_endtoend} of them — under the historical AND the published constants — and agrees with X3C; every free hex within L∞ < {sep_required} of a deployment stub lies in its own element's region ({stub_near_hexes} hexes on the corpus; the nearest free hex outside the stub's own vertex box is at L∞ {stub_margin_min}, which is why step 5 of Lemma D.4 no longer says nothing lies within that distance)

Lemma D.4 step 5, the deployment-stub clause: every used-port set of a vertex box (at most three ports) × every unused stub direction × both row parities, adjacency from the model's own neighbour rule — {stub_cases} local configurations
0 failures: the outer stub hex has exactly one free neighbour in every case
{hp_objective_instances} instances ({hp_objective_yes} yes, {hp_objective_no} no), plus a negative control
every optimum certified over the full action model; the ghost bound also dominates every `(‡)` play (see `paper/companion-empirics.md`)
every score certified likewise, and reproduced exactly by the `(‡)` phase-aware replay
all equal the recorded optima; `--legacy-defend` reproduces the {legacy_round5_violations} round-5 violations (negative control)

the three suites above re-run twice: every damage call evaluated in Python floats AND in the exact rationals of Section 2 of the paper ({exact_calls} calls, {exact_fractional} with a fractional factor), then with the exact routine installed outright

{exact_splits} call-level splits, each a float result one point below the exact one, none on a deciding branch: all {empirical_instances} optima, their `(‡)` replays and all {scored_responses} scores are reproduced exactly under exact arithmetic; positive control (float 62 vs exact 63) detected

{regressions} regressions: one per error ever caught here, a phase-ordered trace of the capped defended branch, and a doc-consistency battery that re-renders this very table into README.md from its manifest, re-runs the generating suites to pin the manifest's counters (only the two `--full` Theorem 3 tiers excepted — those are swept against the proof document), sweeps the counter prose in the siblings, the paper body and the companion note, and bans {banned_claims} retired claims verbatim
{engine_exact} exact, {engine_explained} explained (Section 4.2 of the paper); includes {engine_turn_order_cases} turn-order cases run through the engine's own `battleGetTurnOrder`
